summary: Intermittent 429 waves after edge TLS offload causing delayed token refill for mixed realtime and scheduled flushes
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (BrightPath Health, dedicated pool) report recurring 429 spikes concentrated around scheduled background flush windows (cron flush at :15 and :45) and intermittent realtime chat traffic. The spikes correlate with a ~10-20s delay between observed edge connection handoffs (TLS offload on edge-proxy) and the token/refill accounting update reaching the central rate-limiter, causing tenant token buckets to appear depleted and reject inbound requests.

Impact:
- Customer observes elevated 429s for both low-latency interactive chat and batch flush workers for ~30-90s windows.
- Affects revenue-impacting features for a production dedicated tenant.
- Customer-tier SLA is at risk if not mitigated.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool fronted by edge-proxy cluster in prod-us-west.
- Ingress: edge-proxy performs TLS termination and then proxies to origin pool.
- Rate limiter uses epoched refill messages from edge to central accounting service.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer runs scheduled background flush at HH:15 and HH:45 and keeps a small percentage of realtime traffic running.
2) Edge-proxy rotates TLS sessions due to cert rekey or client rehandshake; connection is briefly torn down and re-established on a different edge node.
3) In 10-20s after handshake, requests begin receiving 429s despite console showing available burst credits.
4) Token refill from new edge node arrives delayed; after refill is applied, requests succeed.

Observed logs and metrics:
- edge-proxy logs: repeated TLS session reassignments and upstream connection resets around the event times. (See log excerpt: edge-proxy/2026-03-12T15:45:10Z: "session assigned node-12 -> node-7; upstream-reset; refill-msg queued")
- rate-limiter metrics: spike in per-tenant rejections, refill apply latency increased from median 120ms to P95 ~15s at the incident times.
- console credit UI: shows eventual correct burst credits after a lag that matches refill apply latency.

Additional context:
- Customer confirmed they rotated a signing cert on their side earlier that day, which increased short-lived TLS renegotiations for a subset of clients.
- Dedicated pool is configured with a small refill grace window to prevent double-counting during edge handoffs. The grace logic appears to be mis-triggering in the TLS-offload+connection-reassign case and delaying the refill application longer than intended.
comments: Support (Ava Martinez) 2026-03-12: Received alert from BrightPath Support rep via #support. Reproduced initial 429 pattern in logs. Escalated to SRE and assigned to Liam.

Customer (BrightPath) 2026-03-12: We're seeing user-facing errors exactly during our scheduled flush windows. Console shows credits available but requests still 429. This started after our cert rotation earlier today.

SRE (Liam Chen) 2026-03-12: Confirmed spike in refill-apply latency on rate-limiter. Edge-proxy logs show TLS session handoffs ~10s prior to rejections. Opening investigation. Slack channel #incidents/SUP-864321 created.

Engineering (Ritika Patel) 2026-03-12: Hypothesis: refill messages are being deduped or queued after handshake due to grace window logic in edge-to-limiter handshake path. Will instrument message trace IDs to follow refill flow.
Support (Ava Martinez) 2026-03-13: Customer requests temporary mitigation to reduce user impact while fix is developed.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and trace findings:
- 2026-03-12T15:44:55Z: edge-proxy node-12 closes client TLS session and proxies to node-7 (log id: ep-evt-9952).
- 2026-03-12T15:45:04Z: client reconnects; node-7 sends refill message for tenant T-1442 but the central accounting service logs a grace-check that delays applying the refill until 15:45:20Z due to inferred duplicate-event protection.
- Refill apply lag correlates with implementation that defers applying refills for up to 15s when an edge node reports recent activity to avoid double-counting from reconnections. The logic is conservative and does not correctly detect TLS-offload handoff scenario, causing unnecessary delay.
- Trace instrumentation added via PR github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/1120 shows refill message idempotency keys missing when edge proxy reassigns session, leading to code path that queues instead of immediate-apply.

Hypotheses tested:
- Hypothesis A: Cert rotation increased frequency of reassigns and tripped grace window. Confirmed by correlation with customer's cert rotation time.
- Hypothesis B: Healthcheck traffic being misattributed to tenant causing refill noise. Not substantiated in logs.

Temporary mitigation attempts:
- Increased refill-apply aggressiveness for the affected tenant in a canary flag (applied at 2026-03-12T18:00Z) reduced 429 window from ~30-90s to ~5-10s but carries minor double-counting risk; rolled back for general population but held for BrightPath as a temporary measure with informed consent.
resolution_notes:
Short-term mitigation:
- Enabled tenant-scoped override to bypass the conservative refill delay for BrightPath (effective 2026-03-12T18:15Z). 429 incidence dropped to baseline during next scheduled flush. Customer confirmed reduced user impact.

Long-term fix plan:
- Engineering will land three items: 1) edge-proxy will include stable session trace IDs on refill messages during node reassignment, 2) rate-limiter will use trace ID to immediately dedupe and apply refill when trace ID indicates a handoff rather than an unknown duplicate, 3) tune grace window logic to be adaptive based on variance in refill latency.
- Related PRs and tasks: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1034 (add session-trace-header), github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/1123 (apply-on-trace-match), internal task INT-4321 to adjust grace-window heuristics.

Estimated rollout timeline:
- PRs targeted for review by 2026-03-16, canary rollout to prod-us-west by 2026-03-18, full rollout by 2026-03-22 after monitoring.

Customer follow-up:
- CS scheduled check-in with BrightPath for 2026-03-14 to confirm behavior during scheduled flush and to share postmortem once fix is deployed.
next_steps: Engineering to merge PRs and add automated e2e test for TLS-offload handoff (owner: Ritika Patel)
SRE to monitor refill-apply latency dashboards and alert on P95 > 2s for affected tenant (owner: Liam Chen)
CS to coordinate customer check-in and document temporary bypass agreement in account notes (owner: Ava Martinez)
Postmortem to be drafted after full rollout and linked in this ticket (owner: Liam Chen)
